card.title: J2M RAIDEN
card.text: Gets +1+1 and -1 operation cost when the enemy gives an order.
card.flavorText: The Mitsubishi J2M Raiden, meaning “Lightning Bolt,” was a land-based interceptor developed for the Imperial Japanese Navy Air Service. Designed by Jiro Horikoshi, who had also created the A6M Zero, the Raiden represented a different approach to fighter design. It was intended primarily to intercept high-altitude bombers, prioritizing speed, climbing ability, and heavy armament over the exceptional manoeuvrability associated with earlier Japanese fighters. Development was slowed by problems with engine cooling and the undercarriage, and combat units did not begin receiving the improved J2M3 in significant numbers until early 1944. The Raiden made its combat debut during the Battle of the Philippine Sea in June 1944 and was later used chiefly in the defense of Japan against B-29 Superfortress raids. Armed with four 20 mm guns, it carried formidable firepower. Pilots used dive and zoom attacks to compensate for reduced performance at extreme altitude. Limited production and the American shift toward night-bombing further reduced its effectiveness. Nevertheless, Raidens were still fighting on 15 August 1945, only hours before Japan announced its surrender.
